title: Minimal source-change re-fetch check (hash-diff) [automated in M1]
context: Clinical guidance changes. A QPL set grounded in NCI/PDQ content that was accurate when authored may become misleading if the source page is silently updated. The source allow-list (qpl-sources-001) records snapshotHash (SHA-256) values for each source; the watcher re-fetches those sources and compares the current hash to the recorded one, flagging any drift for re-verification. M0 requires only a minimal, manually-run script; M1 (qpl-watcher-002) will schedule it. This is a safety feature, not a nice-to-have: undetected source drift is listed as a high-impact risk in the PLAN.
objective: Write scripts/check-sources.ts (or similar) — a minimal, manually-run script that reads sources/allow-list.yaml, re-fetches each source at its canonical URL, computes the SHA-256 of the response, and compares it to the recorded snapshotHash; prints a DRIFT report for any entry where the hash differs and exits non-zero if any drift is detected. Wire it into the repo so a maintainer can run it with a single command.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-sources.ts (or equivalent) is present and reads all entries from sources/allow-list.yaml
For each entry, the script fetches the canonical URL, computes SHA-256 of the response body, and compares it to the recorded snapshotHash field; outputs MATCH or DRIFT per entry
The script exits non-zero and prints a clear DRIFT DETECTED summary if any source hash differs from the recorded value; prints ALL SOURCES MATCH if none differ
The script handles network errors gracefully (prints FETCH-ERROR per entry, does not crash; exits non-zero if any entry could not be checked)
A one-line run instruction is added to CONTRIBUTING.md or the repo README so the maintainer knows how to run it
The script does not commit or overwrite snapshotHash values automatically — it only reports; re-verification and hash update are a manual maintainer step
pnpm build and pnpm test pass after this change
resources: packages/schema/src/schemas.ts (qpl-schema-001 — sourceAllowListSchema defines the YAML shape)
PLAN.md (Source-change check; Security section; Risk row for 'Outdated guidance')
output: scripts/check-sources.ts (or equivalent); updated CONTRIBUTING.md or README with run instruction; PR to the repo
